why: Item 1 is avoided. Check 3 reads the export list from math.js and requires a README match for each function, and its FAIL condition names subtract. A README that documents clamp but not subtract therefore fails. Checks 1, 2 and 4 stay within their lines: there is no exact error message, no parameter count, and boundary or float cases are still covered by "limited to the range". Item 2 breaks in Check 3. Its PASS needs "the script reports nothing missing", and the script matches each name only with the regex `\bname\s*\(`, so the name must be followed by an opening parenthesis. A README that documents subtract in another valid form, such as a table row "| `subtract` | returns a minus b |" or "`subtract` — subtracts b from a", would FAIL. That makes the check depend on a specific README format, which is stricter than "README.md documents every function math.js exports".
